opening.text: Your front door works like a market table — nine photographs of pots, three sentences about the firing, and a menu where buying and reading are the same size.

positioning_legibility.observation: Slow pots for daily use tells a cold visitor, in one second, what you make and how you expect it to be lived with.

tangibles.observation: Thrown, fired and packed by me is the most concrete line on the first screen, and it describes your labour, not an object with a size and a sum.

exhibit.quote: Everything here is thrown, fired and packed by me in a workshop behind the house in Bridnall.
exhibit.speaker: owner

entry_point.observation: Five doors sit in the menu at one weight, the one that sells pots looks like the one that explains you, and nothing is marked as the place to start.

exhibit.reference: the five-door menu across the top, running Home, Shop, Workshops, About, Contact
exhibit.speaker: not_applicable

delivered_vs_handheld.observation: A visitor leaves holding a feeling about ash and wood fire. They don’t leave holding a size, a date, or a way to pay you.

exhibit.reference: the nine photographs of pots below the text, and the footer under them
exhibit.speaker: not_applicable

gap.what_you_have: A wood kiln lit since 2011, five months at the Fennhollow residency, and a shelf at Marrow and Grain since 2019.
gap.what_a_stranger_gets: The pots and the town, and there’s nobody but you saying the work is any good.

named_facts.source_sentence: In 2018 I spent five months at the Fennhollow residency in Cumbria, learning to fire with wood.

named_facts.source_sentence: My mugs and jars are stocked by Marrow and Grain in Ellisford, and have been since 2019.

surfaces_searched: the footer on all four pages

rejected.reason: The two Saturdays on the Workshops page are both still ahead; nothing dated sits behind them on the homepage, the Shop page or the About page.

lane_verdicts.evidence: One kiln, lit since 2011, still the only one you use, and it’s on the front page in your own words before anyone scrolls.
lane_verdicts.bold_line: Your front page already carries the reason to trust the pots.

exhibit.quote: My mugs and jars are stocked by Marrow and Grain in Ellisford, and have been since 2019.
exhibit.speaker: owner

lane_verdicts.evidence: Fennhollow and the shelf at Marrow and Grain are the two facts that settle a nervous buyer, and both sit on your About page. That shop is your only second voice, and it speaks to whoever thinks to look.

exhibit.quote: Your pots go into the next wood firing and arrive by post about a month later.
exhibit.speaker: owner

lane_verdicts.evidence: Your Workshops page is the one place where something ends with a person holding an object: a Saturday, a wheel, and pots posted after the next firing. You sequence a workshop day better than you sequence the room a visitor walks into.

exhibit.reference: the single line about ash falling differently on every shelf of the kiln
exhibit.speaker: not_applicable

lane_verdicts.evidence: No sentence here explains what you learned at that kiln, only what comes out of it.
lane_verdicts.bold_line: Everything you know about wood firing lives in conversation with you.

one_cut.text: The kiln made it onto your front page; the shop that has sold your mugs since 2019 did not.

bridge.text: A visitor cannot buy a mug, see what one costs, or put a name against a firing date without emailing you and waiting. The Workshops page already knows how to end with someone holding an object; nothing else on your site does.
